entities.summary: Jaume Serra i Cau was a Spanish Valencian cardinal who played a pivotal role in the intricate web of power politics within the Catholic Church during the 16th century. As tutor to the young Giovanni Borgia, he became embroiled in the complex machinations of the Borgias, whose rise and fall would shape the course of European history. Serra i Cau's influence extended beyond the Vatican, as he navigated the treacherous landscape of Renaissance politics, forging alliances and negotiating power struggles that would have far-reaching consequences. His legacy as a master of intrigue and diplomacy has been eclipsed by the grandeur of his contemporaries, yet his contributions to the Church's inner workings remain a testament to his cunning and strategic acumen. The oft-overlooked figure of Jaume Serra i Cau stands as a reminder that even in the most obscure corners of history, the threads of power and influence can weave together to shape the fabric of human civilization.
